title: Roguish Life
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's rustic self-defense against aristocratic delicacy.

title: Count the Steps of Life
text:
Of disgusting matter I was formed,

conceived in the shackles of a fault,

condemned to die without having been born,

for I am unborn and already buried.


Freed from the dark narrowness,

I emerge an unformed, unknown clod,

for the only sign that I breathe is a groan,

a melancholy report of my state.


I open my eyes, and the first thing I see

is that the sphere too is a dark prison;

I know the final end must arrive.


Then where does my madness guide me,

if from being to dying I am a prisoner,

in the womb, in the world, and in the grave?
editorial_note: The translation keeps life as a sequence of prisons: womb, world, and sepulcher.

title: Reply to Phyllis
text:
Wretched, poor, alone, and beaten down,

I live in this unhappy populated wasteland,

and since being unfortunate is no choice,

I am ashamed of being so unfortunate.


Reason is of no use, nor has it been useful

to one ruled by the cruelty of fate,

for care is sometimes unhappy,

as negligence is sometimes glorious.


In ordering me to live joyfully,

you add more torments to my fears,

for I cannot, Phyllis, be obedient.


How shall I be able to hide from displeasures

if each person is martyr to the evil he feels,

and no one is architect of his tastes?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the reply's refusal of cheerful obedience under fate and temperament.

title: He Writes to Absent Lesbia...
text:
I rise early at the day's first light,

after a light and measured sleep,

and sleep has only this heaviness:

not sleeping with your eyes, my Lesbia.


This obstinacy follows me inseparably,

my contemplation and your care,

in the house, on the mountain and in the meadow,

and in the warmest and the coldest season;


at table I contemplate your face,

night comes and I see you plainly;

for even though my loving soul reproaches me,


how can it believe that you are absent,

if there is no hour, minute, or instant

in which it does not see you very present?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the absent beloved as continuously present in the speaker's perception.

title: The Payment the World Gives to Poets
text:
They say of Quevedo that he was clear

and that in some verses he is obscene;

Góngora may well have been good,

but now his commentaries make him strange.


Calderón, whom they sell us dearly,

was only very full of love matters,

and left us in comedy a poison

that we have drunk without hesitation.


Juan Pérez's idea was lowly,

Solís's tangled; unhappy fate!

O poor science! Lost faculty!


Drunken world, which to the strongest man,

after miserably wearing him down in life,

preaches these honors in his death!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the literary criticism and the bitter contrast between living neglect and posthumous honor.
